levelMapping: NVIDIA uses an internal IC1-IC9 ladder. An NVIDIA employee on Blind (Jan 2025): IC3 = 3-5 YOE, IC4 = 5-8, IC5 = 8-12; external 'Senior Software Engineer' postings fill at IC3 or IC4 depending on interview performance (IC3->IC4 takes 3-4 years internally). At ~3.3 YOE expect IC3 (~Google L4); a 10-YOE India senior system-software candidate was told IC4. Some prep sites show a shifted table (IC2 = 2-5 YOE), so confirm the req's level with the recruiter - final level is partly set by loop performance.

process.summary: Team-led and deliberately unstandardised: recruiters are vague, there is no central rubric, and each interviewer asks what their team cares about. Common skeleton for software roles: recruiter screen -> HackerRank OA (most India and early-career reqs) -> 1-2 technical phone screens (resume deep-dive plus live coding with constraint-tightening follow-ups) -> virtual onsite of 3-6 back-to-back 45-60 min rounds (coding, C/C++/OS fundamentals and domain deep dive, system design for mid-level+ backend/infra reqs, behavioral/manager) -> an in-person visit, which policy requires before any offer. Coding skews LC easy-medium but must compile and run: several 2026 rounds were practical tasks on a live VM or debugging provided buggy code, and interviewers often refuse library shortcuts and ask you to hand-roll the data structure. The real bar is depth: your own projects (probed 15-45 min in almost every round), C/C++ memory behaviour, concurrency, and the team's domain (CUDA/GPU, drivers, networking, Kubernetes/cloud).

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, why NVIDIA/this team, location, notice period, comp. NVIDIA encourages applying to up to five matching roles; parallel team loops are normal but feedback may be shared across teams.
rounds.probes: Resume-vs-req fit. Recruiters usually cannot say what rounds will cover ('all interviews are technical in nature') - ask the hiring manager instead.

rounds.name: Online assessment (HackerRank)
rounds.what: 2-3 coding problems (LC easy-medium, occasionally one harder) plus MCQs on C/C++ output, pointers, OS (threads, deadlock, memory, scheduling) and sometimes aptitude/probability. Video-proctored; unapproved AI tools disqualify. India on-campus variants: ~28-50 MCQs + 2 coding in 60-90 min.
rounds.probes: Speed and from-scratch implementation; MCQ section is often rated harder than the coding. Some senior/experienced loops skip the OA and go straight to a screen.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen (x1-2)
rounds.what: 10-15 min resume/project deep dive, then live coding on HackerRank CodePair or CoderPad: one LC easy-medium problem or a C/C++-flavoured implementation task (string class, hash map without STL, memcpy, KV store). Some teams run it as 90 min with two interviewers.
rounds.probes: Follow-ups tighten constraints: make it thread-safe, make it faster, input no longer fits in memory, complexity stated unprompted. C/C++ roles probe memory layout, cache effects, pointers.

rounds.name: Hiring manager round
rounds.what: Behavioral plus high-level technical: walk through your most complex project, trade-offs, role expectations. In India this often lands at the END of the loop as a 'managerial round' and can include a DSA/DP question and scenario questions.
rounds.probes: Scope of ownership, why this team, career plans. Good moment to ask what the onsite rounds will cover - the HM sets the agenda.

rounds.name: Onsite: coding
rounds.what: 1-2 problems per session, LC easy-medium with hard follow-ups; arrays/strings, linked lists, trees/graphs, sliding window, heaps. Some teams swap one coding round for a debugging exercise on provided buggy code.
rounds.probes: Hand-rolled data structures over std:: shortcuts, clean compilable code, edge cases, narrated reasoning. Verbal-only answers to follow-ups are often scored as not done.

rounds.name: Onsite: fundamentals / domain deep dive
rounds.what: C/C++ (output questions, virtual functions, smart pointers, std::move, alignment, structure padding), OS (mutex vs semaphore, deadlock, virtual memory, scheduling, interrupts), architecture (cache hierarchy, endianness, RISC vs CISC), and team domain: CUDA/GPU basics, drivers, networking (ARP/STP/LAG for Mellanox-side teams), Kubernetes/Docker/CI-CD for cloud/infra teams.
rounds.probes: Depth on whatever you claim: 'prove you have done this'. India loops also mix in puzzles (torch-and-bridge, 10-coins heads/tails split, ants on a triangle, ABCD x 4 = DCBA).

rounds.name: Onsite: system design
rounds.what: For mid-level+ backend/infra/cloud reqs. Performance-flavoured prompts (inference serving, cluster control plane, telemetry, CI pipelines, artifact stores) rather than design-Twitter. Several teams, including some 2026 loops, run NO system design at all - driver/embedded loops replace it with domain discussion.
rounds.probes: Throughput, latency, memory budget, GPU utilisation, failure recovery, back-of-envelope numbers; defending trade-offs under pushback.

rounds.name: Onsite: practical coding
rounds.what: Some teams (2026 reports): a live VM inside HackerRank where you write a real program (collect CPU/memory/disk metrics, POST JSON to the interviewer's server, debug a 403; fetch a paginated HTTP API and filter records). Googling basics was tolerated; running out of time was not.
rounds.probes: Working end-to-end code within 45 min; HTTP/JSON handling, /proc parsing, methodical debugging of the failing request.

rounds.name: Onsite: behavioral
rounds.what: STAR stories mapped to NVIDIA values (intellectual honesty, speed and agility, one team): a mistake and what changed, cross-team conflict, negative feedback, tight deadline. Often folded into the HM/director round; one 2026 loop opened with a director doing BQ plus deep dives across ALL past jobs.
rounds.probes: Honest ownership of errors (no hero endings), cross-functional examples, mentorship for senior band.

process.indiaNotes: India hires SWE/Senior SWE across Bengaluru, Pune and Hyderabad (networking/Mellanox and infra teams concentrated in Bengaluru, graphics/QA presence in Pune). The India loop leans harder on the HackerRank OA, C/C++/OS fundamentals, aptitude MCQs and puzzles than US loops; system design appears mainly for backend/cloud reqs. Round counts vary wildly: a Nov 2025 Bengaluru SWE reported EIGHT rounds (binary search, distributed task scheduler, priority queue, Python fundamentals, concurrency, managerial last); a GFG SDE-2 loop had 5 rounds including a logic/probability round; a Pune Mar 2025 candidate was rejected after solving everything, suspecting partial code written only verbally. A Bengaluru networking loop (Aug 2026) was almost entirely ARP/LAG/STP/MLAG/TCP-UDP plus C array drills. Expect slow HR: offer letters delayed ~2 months for budget approval (2024 report), positions put on hold mid-pipeline (Feb 2025), and ghosting between rounds.
process.timeline: Official line: decision within weeks of first interview. Reports: 1-2 weeks (fast teams, one 'offer in five days, five back-to-back rounds') to 2 months (Tel Aviv home-exam loop); 4-8 weeks typical; silence of 3-5+ weeks after onsite is normal; senior offers need director/VP sign-off and committee review every ~2 weeks.
tips: Prep the team, not the company: read the JD line by line, ask the HM what each onsite round covers - they usually tell you.
Expect to hand-roll data structures in C/C++/Python without library shortcuts (LRU without OrderedDict, hash map without STL).
Write code that compiles and runs; finish follow-ups in code - verbal-only answers were counted as failures in 2026 reports.
Know your resume cold: every round starts with a project deep dive, and senior loops probe older jobs too.
Drill OS + C/C++ fundamentals (mutex vs semaphore, deadlock, virtual memory, vtables, std::move, alignment, cache lines) even for application-level roles.
For backend/cloud reqs (DGX Cloud, NGC, GeForce NOW), be fluent in Kubernetes, Docker, CI/CD image flow and distributed-systems basics.
Practice performance-flavoured design (inference serving, schedulers, telemetry) instead of design-Twitter templates.
Prepare value-mapped behavioral stories: a real mistake (intellectual honesty), cross-team work (one team), shipping fast.
Do not use AI tools in any round - stated grounds for disqualification.
Interviewing with multiple NVIDIA teams at once is fine and common; a reject lets you re-interview with another team immediately.
process.notes: OA platform is HackerRank (video-proctored; CodePair for live rounds, CoderPad on some teams). Company policy requires an in-person onsite before an offer. No bar-raiser or central committee per team - scorecards go to a hiring committee meeting ~biweekly, and any single weak round can sink the loop. No team-matching phase: you interview with the exact team. The LeetCode NVIDIA tag is only loosely predictive - a Feb 2026 candidate reported grinding it 'didn't help'; fundamentals and the practical 'must compile and run' bar matter more. LLD exists but as C++/concurrency implementation rounds (ring buffer, shared_ptr, allocator, string class) rather than a formal machine-coding round; see lld[].

dsa.variant: O(n) deque solution expected; candidate had accepted offer.
dsa.evidence: Glassdoor SWE report (2026-05, offer); also high in NVIDIA LC tag 6-mo window.

dsa.variant: Recurs with twists: thread-safe follow-up, serialization + evolving constraints, eviction-order twist in a 90-min OA, and no-STL/hand-rolled DLL versions.
dsa.evidence: Aced phone-screen pool, Career Drill OA report (2025-08), PracHub listing (2026-02), OphyAI/SpaceComplexity guides.

dsa.title: Top K Frequent Elements
dsa.variant: Asked as streaming top-K: interviewer rejected the heap answer and pushed for O(1) add via count buckets; also as top-N from a log stream, and in a 90-min OA.
dsa.evidence: PracHub screen report (2026-06), PracHub onsite listing (2026-09), Career Drill OA (2025-08).

dsa.variant: Also asked to a senior data-infra candidate; TechPrep lists it among most-reported NVIDIA problems.
dsa.evidence: PracHub listing (2026-05), Aced pool, TechPrep guide.

dsa.variant: Paired with bracket validation and a small HTTP/API task in one screen; 100% of NVIDIA LC-tag votes in the 6-mo window.

dsa.title: Count substrings with no repeated characters
dsa.statement: Count all non-empty contiguous substrings of a lowercase string (up to 1e5 chars) that contain no repeated character. Counting variant of LC 3: for each right end, add the window length; handle equal characters correctly.
dsa.variant: Senior+ round; brute force rejected for the 1e5 bound.

dsa.title: Group Anagrams
dsa.variant: Asked in a two-part round with an in-place memory-allocator task; also 87.5% in LC-tag 3-mo window.

dsa.evidence: PracHub listings (2025-10), GFG FW-developer round 1 (2024-03), Aced pool.

dsa.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
dsa.variant: O(n)-time requirement stated; older system-software round demanded the O(1)-space interleaving trick.
dsa.evidence: Glassdoor firmware round, Haifa (2026-09); GFG system-software experience.

dsa.title: Add Two Numbers
dsa.variant: Round-2 question in a 4-round India loop that ended in an offer.

dsa.title: Build a tree from parent-child pairs and find the root
dsa.statement: Given a list of (parent, child) node pairs, identify the root and construct the tree by linking all nodes; then answer traversal follow-ups.

dsa.title: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal
Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
dsa.variant: Reported in recent onsites; the simpler 'top view of binary tree' variant also appears.

Word Pattern
dsa.variant: The single coding question of a 45-min distributed-systems phone screen; candidate rejected two days later despite solving it.
dsa.evidence: Glassdoor System SWE Distributed Systems screen (2025-01).

dsa.title: Isomorphic Strings
dsa.variant: One of five problems in a 90-min OA.

dsa.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
dsa.variant: Same 90-min OA.

dsa.title: Course Schedule
dsa.variant: Framed as 'detect a cycle in a directed graph' in the OA; topological-sort pseudocode also asked live in older loops.

dsa.title: Continuous Subarray Sum
dsa.variant: Subarray of length >= 2 summing to a multiple of k.

dsa.title: Encode and Decode Strings
dsa.variant: Serialize/deserialize a list of strings that may contain digits and symbols; asked in both screens and onsites.

dsa.title: Valid Palindrome
dsa.variant: One of three take-home HackerRank problems before a Yoqne'am onsite.

dsa.title: Reorganize String
dsa.variant: Asked as 'shuffle a playlist so no two consecutive songs share an artist', ordering by artist frequency.

dsa.title: O(1) init/get/set/reset array
dsa.statement: Design a data structure over an array supporting constant-time initialization, get(i), set(i, v) and reset-all. Classic constant-time-initialization trick with a generation counter or stack of touched slots.
dsa.variant: Asked verbally at the end of an onsite day.

dsa.title: Maximize Greatness of an Array
dsa.variant: Named OA problem in a 2025 on-campus drive (plus a custom bitwise recurrence problem); also in the NVIDIA LC tag.

dsa.title: Find The Original Array of Prefix Xor
dsa.variant: OAs repeatedly feature XOR/bitwise subarray problems (IGNITE and intern OAs); this tag problem matches the reports.
dsa.evidence: Glassdoor IGNITE OA reports (2026-04); NVIDIA LC tag.

dsa.title: Missing Number
dsa.variant: Asked with 'optimize it' follow-up in a firmware round; also in the NVIDIA LC tag.

dsa.title: Number of 1 Bits
dsa.variant: Count set bits two ways and compare trade-offs (loop vs n&(n-1) vs lookup).

dsa.title: Min Stack
dsa.variant: NVIDIA variant demands O(1) getMin with O(1) EXTRA space (encoded-difference trick), not the easy two-stack version.
dsa.evidence: GFG SDE-2 loop (2022); still 75% in NVIDIA LC-tag 6-mo window (2026).

dsa.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
dsa.variant: Also asked as find-minimum (LC 153) with binary search expected; binary-search variants recur across India loops.
dsa.evidence: GFG SDE-2 loop (2022), GFG system-software experience, TechPrep guide, Glassdoor Bengaluru 8-round loop mention of binary search (2025-11).

dsa.title: Matrix transpose + key-value store with setAll
dsa.statement: Phone screen for a Linux-oriented role, multiple tasks: (1) transpose an n x n matrix; (2) design an OO key-value store with set(key, v), get(key) and setAll(v) where setAll updates every existing key - expected average O(1) per op via a global timestamp/generation instead of touching every key; (3) spot bugs in a short C snippet.

dsa.title: Count distinct strings with a hand-built hash table, then parallelize
dsa.statement: GPU search-engine team screen: count distinct strings in an array with NO library containers (write the hash table yourself), then make it parallel-safe. Candidate used atomic counters plus a shared/exclusive lock on miss; interviewer steered toward open addressing (GPU-friendly). Follow-up: how to split 1M keys across threads with memory-adjacent access.

dsa.title: Collect CPU/memory/disk metrics and POST as JSON
dsa.statement: Onsite on a live VM inside HackerRank: write a real program that reads the machine's CPU, memory and disk usage (/proc etc.), packs it into JSON and POSTs it to the interviewer's server; debug the 403 the server returns. Follow-up: check readings against a threshold before sending (framed as a simple sliding-window check). Googling basics was allowed; unfinished code counted against the candidate.

dsa.title: Fetch paginated medical records and filter by rules
dsa.statement: 45-min screen: pull all records from a paginated HTTP endpoint (10 per page, unknown page count), apply a long list of field-comparison conditions, and one condition comparing each record's weight against the patient's historical average, which you must compute from the data. Spec is long; working code expected; handle missing/badly-typed fields and retries.

dsa.title: Merge sorted arrays, then external-sort N huge files
dsa.statement: Onsite: start with the easy two-pointer merge of two sorted integer sequences, then scale twice - (1) both inputs and the output are files too big for memory (streaming merge, bounded buffers, crash safety), (2) N such files must be globally sorted and stored (k-way merge / external sort, range partitioning across machines, skew handling).

dsa.title: Implement memcpy and memmove
dsa.statement: Write memcpy from scratch, then explain and handle overlapping ranges (memmove semantics, copy direction). Follow-ups: word-at-a-time copying, alignment.
dsa.evidence: GFG FW-developer round 2 (2024-03); Aced phone-screen pool.

dsa.title: Design a simple hash map without STL
dsa.statement: Implement a hash map from scratch (buckets, collision policy, resize) without library containers; discuss load factor and complexity.

dsa.title: Aligned allocation: align_malloc / UP_ALIGN macro
dsa.statement: Two reported forms: implement align_malloc(size, align) returning a pointer rounded to the alignment (e.g. malloc returns 123, align 10 -> 120/130), with the bookkeeping needed to free it; and write an UP_ALIGN(size, align) macro rounding up to the next power-of-two multiple (UP_ALIGN(10, 8) = 16).

dsa.title: Convert 4D tensor layout NCHW to NHWC in a flat array
dsa.statement: A 4-D tensor is stored in a 1-D array in NCHW order; write code to rewrite it in NHWC order (index arithmetic between the two layouts), e.g. N=1, C=3, H=2, W=2.

dsa.title: 32-bit multiplication on a 16-bit ALU
dsa.statement: Write a C program that multiplies two 32-bit integers on a processor whose ALU only supports 16-bit multiplication - split operands into high/low halves, combine partial products with shifts and carries. The candidate who could not finish it was rejected.

dsa.title: In-order traversal with explicit stack, then optimize
dsa.statement: Implement iterative in-order traversal using a stack (LC 94 without recursion), state time/space complexity, then discuss optimizing space (Morris traversal direction).

dsa.title: All file paths in an in-memory file-system tree (DFS)
dsa.statement: Given an in-memory file-system tree (nodes with name, isFile, children), return the full path of every file via DFS.

dsa.title: nth prime number
dsa.statement: Return the n-th prime (1-indexed), efficient for moderately large n - sieve with an upper-bound estimate rather than trial division. Related: LC 204 Count Primes is in the NVIDIA tag.

dsa.title: SQL: total city population across joined tables
dsa.statement: Given country/state/city/zip relational tables, write SQL to sum population per city name across joins. One screen also asked the candidate to design a SQL table schema outright.

dsa.title: C/C++ output and language-internals drill
dsa.statement: Rapid-fire, reported across many rounds: predict output of snippets with constructors/destructors, copy constructors, virtual functions (and how vtables work), ++/-- expressions; static vs dynamic libraries; static variables and where they live; delete vs free; std::vector internals; std::move and smart pointers; structure padding and offsetof; function pointers; abstract classes and pure virtual functions.
dsa.evidence: GFG SDE-2 (2022), GFG FW developer (2024-03), GFG internship drives, TechPrep guide (2025-26).

dsa.title: OS and concurrency fundamentals drill
dsa.statement: Reported across screens, onsites and MCQs: mutex vs semaphore; the four deadlock conditions and avoidance; race conditions; user vs kernel mode and system calls; paging, logical vs physical addresses, page/frame math; thread vs process switching; scheduling (preemptive SJF Gantt chart); interrupts; DMA; VM/hypervisor basics vs containers; debugging a production concurrency bug.
dsa.evidence: GFG internship/system-software reports (2023-25), PracHub screen listing (2026-01), Glassdoor Bengaluru 8-round loop (2025-11).

dsa.title: Bit/memory tricks drill
dsa.statement: Set/toggle a given bit; detect little vs big endian in C; determine which way the stack grows; swap two numbers without a temp; reverse bits; convert hex string to decimal; minimum of three numbers without comparison operators.
dsa.evidence: GFG system-software and FW-developer reports (2023-24); PracHub firmware listing (2026-07).

dsa.title: Remove duplicates from an array in C (networking team)
dsa.statement: Bengaluru networking (Mellanox-side) round: remove duplicates from an array in plain C and print the remaining data; the rest of the round was ARP, switch MAC learning, LAG, STP, MLAG and TCP vs UDP.

dsa.title: Debug the provided program
dsa.statement: A recurring round format: you get working-looking code and must find and fix the bugs. Reported forms: a ~250-line C program converting a binary tree to a doubly linked list in spiral order (missing pass-by-reference, stack overflow/underflow checks, bad casts); a Python helper class reading an HTTP stream with concurrency bugs; 'find the error in this Python code' on a screen.
dsa.evidence: GFG compiler-intern round 2 (2024), PracHub listing (2025-08), Glassdoor screen (2025-10, interviewed 2023-01), TechPrep 2025 reports of debugging-only rounds.

lld.title: Multi-producer multi-consumer circular buffer
lld.prompt: Design a fixed-capacity circular buffer for multiple concurrent producers and consumers with blocking put/take and close-and-drain semantics.
lld.deliverable: Working thread-safe code (mutex + condition variables) and reasoning about invariants
lld.evidence: PracHub senior+ listing (2026-07), the most-practiced NVIDIA LLD item there (280+ solves); ring-buffer invariants also probed in firmware rounds.

lld.title: Thread-safe reference-counted smart pointer
lld.prompt: Implement a shared_ptr-style class template from scratch: shared ownership, atomic refcount, copy/move semantics, destruction of the last owner.
lld.deliverable: Compilable C++ class with correct copy/move/destructor behavior
lld.evidence: Two PracHub senior+ listings (2026-08, 2025-09); TechPrep lists it among common NVIDIA LLD prompts.

lld.title: Fixed-pool memory allocator (my_malloc / my_free)
lld.prompt: Given a 32-bit hardware register as a bitmap and a pool of 32 rows x 64 bits, write my_malloc and my_free managing allocations. Part 2: pool grows to 64 rows - manage it with 32-bit registers.
lld.deliverable: Working C code with bit-level bookkeeping
lld.evidence: Glassdoor firmware rounds (2026-10 and 2026-08, one 'declined offer'); TechPrep lists Memory Allocator for systems teams; aligns with align_malloc asked in the SDE-2 loop.

lld.title: Disk-space manager with size-based LRU eviction
lld.prompt: Implement an in-memory disk-space manager storing datasets by id with sizes against a fixed total capacity: put() evicts LRU datasets until the new one fits (error if impossible), get() returns size and refreshes recency; updates adjust used space.
lld.deliverable: Working class/API in any language; LRU by bytes, not count
probes: evicting multiple victims for one put
lld.evidence: PracHub NVIDIA SWE listing (2026-03); cache-with-capacity twists on LRU recur across reports.

lld.title: In-memory VM manager with CRUD API
lld.prompt: Implement a small VM manager: create/list/update/delete VMs (id, name, cpu_cores, memory_gb, status) with unique-id enforcement and consistent error signalling.
lld.deliverable: Working code with data-structure and API-shape justification

lld.title: High-performance string class (small-string optimization)
lld.prompt: Phone screen: implement a string class with cmp/cat/substr over a fixed inline buffer plus heap fallback. Probes: why memcpy beats strncpy, word-at-a-time copies, why short strings compare faster (cache), sizeof the class on 32/64-bit, shrinking the class with a union over buffer/pointer.
lld.deliverable: C++ class written live, constructor first
lld.evidence: PracHub screen report (2025-12) and matching listing; classic NVIDIA C++ screen.

lld.title: Thread-safe / producer-consumer queue
lld.prompt: Implement a thread-safe queue, then a bounded producer-consumer variant with blocking semantics.
lld.deliverable: Working code with mutex/condvar; discuss lock-free option
lld.evidence: TechPrep lists both among common NVIDIA LLD prompts; a 2023 phone screen was 'code a multi-core problem using threads' (Blind).

lld.title: Two threads print numbers in sequence (odd/even)
lld.prompt: Write multithreaded C where one thread prints even and the other odd numbers so output is 0,1,2,3...; interviewer focuses on threads, mutexes and condition variables.
lld.deliverable: Working C code with correct synchronization
lld.evidence: GFG SDE-2 round 4 (2022); concurrency-primitive coding still reported in 2025-26 loops.

lld.title: Cinema ticket reservation system (OOD)
lld.prompt: Model a ticket reservation system for a cinema: entities, seat holds, booking flow.
lld.deliverable: Class design discussion (no full implementation reported)

lld.title: Debugging round: fix the provided program
lld.prompt: You receive a buggy program and must find and fix all issues: a ~250-line C binary-tree-to-DLL-in-spiral converter (call-by-value bug, missing stack overflow/underflow checks, bad casts), or a Python HTTP-stream helper with concurrency bugs.
lld.deliverable: All bugs identified and fixed; code runs
probes: avoiding overflow checks via dynamic structures
lld.evidence: GFG compiler-intern round 2 (2024), PracHub listing (2025-08), TechPrep notes 2025 candidates got debugging-only rounds.

lld.title: Python test harness for graphics validation
lld.prompt: Design a pytest-style harness for graphics validation: fixtures, parametrization across GPU/driver matrix, dependency handling, parallel execution.

lld.title: In-memory file system
lld.prompt: Design an in-memory file system (mkdir, addFile, ls, read) - LC 588 territory; pairs with the reported 'all file paths via DFS' warm-up.
lld.evidence: TechPrep lists it for systems-focused NVIDIA teams.
